briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Regulators Tighten the Screws as James Doubles Down on Hemp; DOJ Presses Chinese Grows and an $8M Clawback
briefs.top: Michigan's Cannabis Regulatory Agency kept up its enforcement push — suspending a hemp processor's license and publishing its latest disciplinary report — as GOP governor hopeful John James broadened his pitch beyond the wholesale tax to cracking down on unregulated hemp sales, even as a second industry lawsuit over the tax's constitutionality grinds toward trial. Nationally, Senate Republicans pressed the DOJ to target Chinese-linked illicit grows, the FDA's psychedelics hearing docket officially closed to comments, Massachusetts voters are bracing for a marijuana-repeal ballot fight, and the feds sued TerrAscend to claw back an $8.3 million tax refund.

local.text: State regulators suspend hemp processor over excess THC — Michigan's Cannabis Regulatory Agency suspended Loud Labs of Michigan's hemp processor-handler license and moved to revoke it after finding delta-9 THC levels above the legal hemp threshold.

CRA publishes its latest disciplinary scorecard — The agency released its August disciplinary action report along with a new report on denied applications and non-renewed licenses across the state's marijuana industry.

James widens his cannabis platform beyond the tax fight — The Republican gubernatorial nominee is now pledging to not only repeal the 24% wholesale tax but also crack down on unregulated, intoxicating hemp sales statewide.

Second lawsuit calls the wholesale tax unconstitutional 'pyramiding' — Mitten Distro X, Refine Michigan and the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association argue the 24% levy inflates the state's 6% sales tax base beyond what the constitution allows.
Whitmer marks October as Substance Misuse Prevention Month — The governor's proclamation cites state data showing 30.1% of young adults in Michigan report current marijuana use.

national.text: GOP senators push DOJ on Chinese-linked illegal grows — Sens. Tom Cotton, Susan Collins, Pete Ricketts and Ted Budd sent Attorney General Todd Blanche a letter urging a crackdown on Chinese criminal networks' role in the illicit cannabis and hemp trade.

FDA's psychedelics comment docket closes — The public comment period following the FDA's September hearing on future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs closed October 5, with input set to inform coordination across the FDA, VA, SAMHSA, NIDA and ARPA-H.

Massachusetts braces for a marijuana repeal vote — Question 8, which would roll back the state's decade-old adult-use law, is headed to the Nov. 3 ballot after a challenge to the petition was rejected, with a recent poll showing 71% of voters opposed.

Maryland's first-responder cannabis protections take effect — A new law signed by Gov. Wes Moore bars employers from disciplining firefighters and rescue workers solely for a positive test tied to off-duty, state-authorized medical cannabis use.

DOJ sues TerrAscend over a disputed 280E refund — The Justice Department's Tax Litigation Branch is seeking to claw back an $8.3 million refund plus interest, arguing the multistate operator wasn't entitled to deductions it claimed under Section 280E.
